BUSINESS IT SERVICES

Managed IT support for businesses.

Managed IT support combines an agreed helpdesk service with defined responsibility for maintaining the systems your team relies on. HeyDock scopes outsourced support for businesses and additional capacity for existing IT departments. The starting point is a review of users, devices, locations and current support arrangements.

Discuss requirementsExplore services

SERVICE EXPLAINED

What does this service involve?

Recurring faults, unclear support ownership and inconsistent device setup can absorb time across a growing team. A managed service creates an agreed route for requests, escalation and planned work. It should also identify what remains with your internal team or existing vendors. A monthly agreement is useful only when the supported environment and service limits are clear.

The engagement starts by identifying the business outcome, existing responsibilities and the changes you authorise. HeyDock then confirms suitable delivery capacity, the working window and the evidence needed to complete the task. Related licences, hardware, subscriptions and specialist services are included only where the proposal says so.

PRACTICAL SCOPE

What can be included?

The final statement of work identifies the tasks that apply to your environment.

Service desk and user support

Define how users report issues, which applications and devices are supported, and who owns each escalation. Requests can then be assessed by business impact rather than simply the order in which messages arrive.

Device and account lifecycle

Scope the joiner, mover and leaver process, including approved device setup, access changes and records. Clearly assigned approval responsibilities help avoid unnecessary access and missed handovers.

Maintenance and service review

Agree the monitoring, patching and reporting actually included in the contract. A review should look at recurring incidents, unresolved risks and upcoming business changes, not just ticket totals.

EXAMPLE REQUIREMENT

How a project might work.

A growing office needs user support but already has a specialist managing its core application. A co-managed arrangement can give HeyDock responsibility for agreed desktop tasks while preserving the existing application escalation route. This is an illustrative engagement, not a customer case study.

PLANNING AND COST

What affects the scope and price?

Cost depends on the number of users, devices or sites; technical complexity; access requirements; delivery hours; travel; and the work needed before and after implementation. Provide relevant system versions and existing supplier responsibilities so the quotation can distinguish labour from licences, equipment and recurring charges.

For a well-defined task, a visit or project quotation may be appropriate. Where important dependencies are unknown, a paid assessment can produce a better implementation scope. Any response, attendance or recovery target must be explicitly agreed; requesting a service does not create an immediate support commitment.

COMMON QUESTIONS

Managed IT support for businesses FAQs

Is managed IT support unlimited?+

Only if a contract explicitly says so. Define users, devices, hours, included work and exclusions before comparing monthly fees.

Can we keep our internal IT team?+

Yes. Co-managed support allocates responsibilities between your team and HeyDock, with escalation and change approval documented.

What information should we include in an enquiry?+

Describe the objective, location, affected systems, preferred timing and existing support arrangements. Do not send passwords or sensitive business records in the enquiry form.
